verdict.rationale: cubic's own CLI reviews local changes before you push, finds bugs, and generates a fix prompt for your coding agent. Cubic also installs into editor-based tools such as Cursor, VS Code and Claude Code, which covers the pre-push, in-editor core of the story. Still, the evidence never says the local review matches the PR review, and the in-editor surface is a CLI plus agent integrations rather than a native IDE review experience. missing for 10: documented parity between local and PR review (same rules, custom agents and memory), a native in-editor review surface beyond the CLI and agent integrations, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I get the same review inside my IDE before I push, catching issues while the code is still in my editor

citations.quote: The cubic CLI reviews local changes before you push. It finds bugs and generates a prompt that your coding agent can use to fix them.
Install and connect cubic in Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or another coding tool.
cubic skills give your coding agent instructions for reviewing code, handling PR comments, and using your team's codebase context.
